purpose: Versioned positive, adversarial, boundary and not-yet-tested cases for the GovCheck evaluator and acceptance adapters.

bindingPolicy.rule: Every executed test must bind its decision to the exact candidate and base/policy context generated or declared by that test.
bindingPolicy.unitTests: Some unit tests use deterministic synthetic candidate/base values and ephemeral keys or policies created by the test. The test source revision is fixed by sourceRevision; runtime-generated cryptographic material is not a production trust root.
bindingPolicy.integrationTests: Git integration tests create exact commit IDs and trust-policy digests at runtime, then verify the exact receive tuple. These tests establish isolated adapter behavior only.
bindingPolicy.production: No fixture or test in this corpus demonstrates a deployed GitHub acceptance boundary or an independently controlled reviewer.

cases.attack: Alter the evaluation report after its digest has been signed.
cases.candidateBinding: Deterministic synthetic candidate revision and content digest in the test; exact report bytes are digested.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Synthetic base revision and governance revision gov-17; trust authority is generated by the test.
cases.limitation: Unit-level decision verifier test; no forge boundary is exercised.

cases.attack: Reuse an otherwise valid decision for a different candidate.
cases.candidateBinding: Deterministic synthetic candidate/base values; test mutates candidate binding.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Synthetic governance revision gov-17 and exact evaluation digest.
cases.limitation: Unit-level binding test.

cases.attack: Accept a report whose underlying evaluation is not PASS without an explicit risk decision.
cases.candidateBinding: Deterministic synthetic candidate and report fixture.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Synthetic governance revision and scope; test policy context.
cases.limitation: Does not establish that a production authority key is correctly controlled.

cases.attack: Tamper with a signed payload or use an unknown key, wrong role or wrong principal.
cases.candidateBinding: Exact candidate binding checked against the signed predicate.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Ephemeral Ed25519 keys and an operator-policy fixture generated by the tests.
cases.limitation: Synthetic keys establish verifier behavior, not real-world identity or key custody.

cases.attack: Use an expired or revoked signing key.
cases.candidateBinding: Exact signed candidate predicate.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Trust-policy fixture contains validity interval and revocation state.
cases.limitation: Key issuance, rotation, incident response and trusted historical timestamps remain outside the provider.

cases.attack: Submit UNKNOWN, FAIL or CONFLICT as an acceptance result.
cases.candidateBinding: Gate tests pass exact repository, VCS, base, candidate and ref values.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Pinned policy revision/digest and verifier identity/digest are supplied by test configuration.
cases.limitation: Tests exercise the local hook protocol, not a live GitHub merge gate.

cases.attack: Replay a decision with a different candidate, base, ref, repository, policy or verifier pin.
cases.candidateBinding: Each mismatch is independently injected into the exact hook tuple.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Repository identity, policy revision/digest and verifier identity/digest are pinned in the test environment.
cases.limitation: The tests use controlled fixtures; no real forge merge candidate is evaluated.

cases.attack: Delete a protected ref or create its initial value through an ordinary receive operation.
cases.candidateBinding: Exact protected ref and old/new object IDs supplied to the hook.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Protected-ref pattern and bootstrap boundary are explicit in the test.
cases.limitation: Bootstrap remains an out-of-band trusted operation.

cases.attack: Treat accepted-with-risk as ordinary PASS or accept it without a complete scoped record and explicit enablement.
cases.candidateBinding: Risk record must match the candidate and protected scope.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Risk acceptance requires explicit deployment enablement and the configured authority/verifier pins.
cases.limitation: A test does not grant risk-acceptance authority in any deployment.

cases.attack: Advance the protected ref after an acceptance decision has been issued, then replay the stale decision.
cases.candidateBinding: A real temporary bare Git repository generates base/candidate commit IDs; the gate checks the exact old/new/ref tuple.
cases.basePolicyBinding: The test generates an ephemeral Ed25519 authority key, trust policy, policy digest and verifier pin.
cases.limitation: Isolated local Git integration only; not GitHub or another hosted forge.

cases.attack: Attempt a protected ref update with UNKNOWN, then retry with an exact PASS decision.
cases.candidateBinding: The test creates a bare remote and exact initial/candidate Git commits.
cases.basePolicyBinding: A pinned fake gate, exact verifier digest, repository identity and policy pin are configured outside the bare repository.
cases.limitation: The integration test proves hook mechanics using a fake verifier; it does not prove semantic correctness or deployment.

cases.attack: Omit required PR/checks, use the wrong status source, enable bypass, or scope a ruleset away from the default branch.
cases.candidateBinding: Ruleset audit fixture names the default branch and expected required-check contexts/source.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Expected approval count, check contexts, source ID and bypass policy are explicit test inputs.
cases.limitation: Read-only configuration audit only; it does not prove that the forge rejects a real update.

cases.attack: Send an update to a ref outside the declared protected-ref set.
cases.candidateBinding: The exact ref is compared with the configured protected-ref patterns.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Protected-ref configuration is explicit; no authorization is inferred for unrelated scopes.
cases.limitation: Non-applicability is local adapter behavior, not proof that the ref is governed by another control.

cases.attack: Append using a stale expected head or race concurrent writers.
cases.candidateBinding: Journal scope and expected head are explicit test values.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Genesis and current journal head are created by the test; actor authenticity is outside this property.
cases.limitation: Single-host SQLite concurrency; not distributed consensus.

cases.attack: Supply duplicate JSON object keys or floating-point values to the canonical journal.
cases.candidateBinding: Exact JSON input bytes are supplied by the test.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Canonicalization profile govcheck.jcs-safe-integer/v1 is fixed by the implementation.
cases.limitation: This does not prove identical parsing behavior in every GovCheck JSON consumer.

cases.attack: Allow publication without a current valid decision, or silently publish through advisory/admin-bypass paths.
cases.candidateBinding: Finite candidate/base values in the TLA+ configuration; no production commit is represented.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Finite policy/verifier constants and BoundaryMode are fixed by the selected TLC configuration.
cases.limitation: A model result applies only to its declared finite abstraction and does not prove implementation refinement.

cases.attack: Change pull-request/push path filters, remove or misroute a reusable workflow, or omit a model-input path so a changed control file does not trigger the intended validation.
cases.candidateBinding: Each test creates an exact synthetic repository tree with workflow files, path filters, reusable-workflow references and model-input files; the test exercises that exact tree.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Each test creates exact synthetic glob/category policy JSON and a TLA category inventory; the test source is pinned by sourceRevision.
cases.limitation: These tests cover the local workflow-routing audit and synthetic path/model-policy fixtures only. They do not prove GitHub ruleset enforcement, a mandatory status-check source, or real protected-ref rejection.

cases.attack: Reuse a TLC/model-checking report from another model revision or configuration.
cases.candidateBinding: The run manifest binds the checked-out commit, model/configuration/reusable-workflow (and discoverable caller-workflow) Git blob IDs, run ID/attempt, and each report's SHA-256 digest and byte length. The verifier rejects source-revision drift, missing or changed reports, and path traversal.
cases.basePolicyBinding: The applicable governance revision and evaluator identity are not yet bound by this manifest; policy freshness remains unknown and cannot be inferred from source freshness.
cases.limitation: Synthetic repository tests exercise source/report freshness rejection. The manifest is unsigned and self-generated by the workflow, so it does not authenticate the hosted run, prevent a compromised workflow from fabricating evidence, bind the applicable governance revision/evaluator, or prove that a required GitHub check is enforced.

cases.attack: Accept a Lean proof artifact containing sorry/admit or an unapproved axiom.
cases.candidateBinding: Future fixture must pin Lean source revision and compiled artifact identity.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Future fixture must pin Lean version, axiom allow-list and audit procedure.
cases.limitation: Existing axiom reports are not yet represented as a negative adversarial candidate corpus.

cases.attack: Attempt a real GitHub protected-ref update through a missing/optional check or an administrator bypass.
cases.candidateBinding: Requires an actual GitHub merge/ref update tied to exact candidate and base revisions.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Requires live ruleset ID, required-check source, approval configuration and bypass actor set.
cases.limitation: Tracked by #45; configuration inspection and local Git tests are not a live GitHub enforcement demonstration.

cases.attack: Publish through a Pijul remote/Nest path that bypasses a local hook.
cases.candidateBinding: Future fixture must pin Pijul change identity and target channel/remote.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Requires a controlled remote/server policy and exact governance revision.
cases.limitation: No mandatory remote Pijul enforcement adapter is implemented.

cases.attack: A repository-controlled build/test/scanner command exfiltrates secrets, accesses host paths or exhausts resources.
cases.candidateBinding: Future fixture must identify the exact candidate tree and invoked command.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Future fixture must pin execution profile, secret set, resource budgets and trusted runner.
cases.limitation: Execution isolation and resource budgets are a new candidate work item; no sandbox is selected.

cases.attack: Treat the report-only GovCheck workflow as a mandatory acceptance check even though the live main ruleset has no required status contexts.
cases.candidateBinding: A real experiment would need the exact pull-request candidate and main base revisions; no protected-ref update was exercised by this corpus case.
cases.basePolicyBinding: Live ruleset Protection Main (ID 28251664) snapshot 2026-11-28 reports an empty required-status-check list; no check-source binding is configured.
cases.limitation: The workflow is explicitly report-only and the live ruleset currently requires zero status checks. This case records the gap; it does not demonstrate a bypass test or rejection. Tracked by #45.
